Periods become longer down the table because additional subshells are filled. Their increasing capacities allow more elements in the longer periods.
Elements in a group generally have the same outermost-shell electronic configuration, so they have the same number of electrons in that shell.
There are four blocks: s, p, d and f. They help in studying element properties because they show which subshell is being filled.

The second and third periods each contain eight elements because only the s and p subshells are filled in those periods. Longer periods also include the filling of d subshells, and the longest include f subshells, allowing 18 or 32 elements.
Mendeleev arranged elements mainly in order of increasing atomic mass, whereas the modern periodic table arranges them in order of increasing atomic number.
